comment: The single source of truth for the support matrix (milestone 8.8, DESIGN.md 4.4, 4.16). The tables in docs/STATUS.md and README.md are generated from it by tools/support_matrix.py; cuervo/script/support.cpp compiles it in (CMake string(JSON)) so the tier and export checks read the same data. Edit this file, then run: python3 -I tools/support_matrix.py --write

levels.title: Stable
levels.meaning: Shipped and covered by the test suite (`ctest`) or a verified end-to-end run. Changes that break it are bugs.

levels.title: Experimental
levels.meaning: Shipped and usable, but with known gaps, limited verification, or an interface that may still change.

levels.title: Planned
levels.meaning: Designed, with a milestone in DESIGN.md section 6, but not in the tree. Do not build on it.

levels.title: Unsupported
levels.meaning: Not provided and not on the near-term roadmap.

entries.name: Linux x86-64, Vulkan 1.3
entries.note: Development and verification platform (Arch Linux; NVIDIA RTX 3060 Ti). Serves both render tiers.

entries.name: Linux x86-64, OpenGL 3.3 core
entries.note: The fallback when there is no Vulkan driver; renders the same scenes as Vulkan (the `rhi_parity` test). Compatible tier only.

entries.name: Linux, OpenGL ES 3.0 (`--gl-es`)
entries.note: The web's shader path, testable on the desktop.

entries.name: Web (WebGPU or WebGL2 / WASM), Chrome
entries.note: Single-threaded by default; WebGPU when the browser has it, else WebGL2 (one build). The shmup reaches the same state hash as the native build on both. See [WEB.md](WEB.md). Compatible tier only.

entries.name: Web, WASM threads
entries.note: Opt-in (`CUERVO_WEB_THREADS`, presets `web-threads` and `web-pack-threads`); the page must be cross-origin isolated.

entries.name: Web, Firefox and Safari
entries.note: Untested; any WebGL2 browser should work.

entries.name: Windows 10/11 x86-64
entries.note: Milestone 10.5a. MSVC, MinGW-w64 GCC and Clang builds have zero warnings and pass the test suite (CI: MSVC Release, MinGW-w64 Debug), and the shmup reaches the Linux state hash on GL and Vulkan. UTF-8 code page and console, per-monitor DPI awareness, a GUI-subsystem player. See [WINDOWS.md](WINDOWS.md).

entries.name: macOS, iOS, Android, consoles
entries.note: Only the long-term Phase 13 mentions them.

entries.name: Vulkan backend
entries.note: Desktop only; supports both render tiers.

entries.name: GL backend (GL 3.3, GLES 3.0, WebGL2)
entries.note: Every RHI feature is implemented in both backends in the same change.

entries.name: `compatible` render tier
entries.note: Promises what WebGL2 offers: 4096 px textures, 4x MSAA, 16 KB uniform ranges. Exports to every target. See Render tiers below.

entries.name: `full` render tier
entries.note: Vulkan on the desktop only. The only Full-only feature today is base-vertex indexed draws; compute, storage buffers and bindless are planned. A Full project on GL or the web is refused. See Render tiers below.

entries.name: Tier migration report (`cuervo-tools tier check`, editor Tier Report)
entries.note: Scans project settings, shaders, scripts, scenes and assets, and checks the claimed tier and target platform against this page.

entries.name: SDF shapes, MSDF text, SVG import (practical subset)
entries.note: Unsupported SVG features (filters, masks, CSS, embedded text) are skipped with a warning.

entries.name: GPU compute visual particles
entries.note: Visual particles run on the CPU on every tier today.

entries.name: Raster processes: images, sprite sheets, atlases, 9-slice, SVG fallback
entries.note: Milestone 11.2a. Art is vector first. PNG, JPEG and QOI import with mip chains, a deterministic atlas packer, sprite-sheet slicing, mips in the RHI on every backend, an instanced sprite batcher, the `Sprite2D`, `AnimatedSprite2D` and `NinePatchRect` nodes, an SVG raster fallback and `.catlas`/`.ctex` in the pack (checked by the `mips` and `sprites` parity scenes on GL, Vulkan and WebGPU). WebP is decoded through libwebp (animated files are rejected). A Chrome smoke covers WebGL2 and WebGPU.

entries.name: Custom user shaders, post-processing
entries.note: Milestone 11.2b. Offscreen render targets and multi-pass, additive and screen blend modes, built-in post passes (bloom, vignette, LUT, CRT) set by `[render.post]`, `[render] color_space = "linear"`, and user `.glsl` shaders with `@export` uniforms compiled by `cuervo-tools shader build` to `.cshader` (SPIR-V, GLES and WGSL). Mesh gradients and light colors are converted in linear mode. Not yet: the editor inspector for `@export` values.

entries.name: SVG rasterized fallback, text shaping (right-to-left, complex scripts)
entries.note: Milestones 11.2a and 11.3. An own SVG rasterizer draws SVG features the vector path does not support into atlases and reports filters and masks instead of drawing them. Text shaping with HarfBuzz, bidirectional text with SheenBidi, Arabic and Japanese fallback fonts and right-to-left layout mirroring work; fallback fonts come from `[text] fallbacks` in `project.toml`, and `LineEdit` and the Split and Scroll containers follow right-to-left layout.

entries.name: 2D lighting (`PointLight2D`, `DirectionalLight2D`, `AmbientLight2D`, `LightOccluder2D`)
entries.note: Milestone 9.7. SDF occluders with raymarched hard and soft shadows, identical on Vulkan and GL; render only (never changes a state hash). Up to 32 lights and 128 occluders per view; see [API.md](API.md).

entries.name: WebGPU
entries.note: Milestones 10.1-10.3: the web default where the browser has it (WebGL2 otherwise, in the same build and in web exports), `--backend webgpu` on Linux (wgpu-native, `CUERVO_WEBGPU`). Every Compatible RHI feature; matches GL in every `rhi_parity` scene and Vulkan exactly, all WGSL generated from GLSL; the shmup and `lantern_cave` reach their native state hashes on WebGPU in headless Chrome, and the browser benchtest (100k shapes, 8 threads) runs stably at 390 FPS (milestone 10.4, [PERFORMANCE.md](PERFORMANCE.md) "Web"). Not in desktop exports. See [WEB.md](WEB.md) "WebGPU".

entries.name: Fixed timestep, seeded PCG32 RNG, deterministic math (`dmath`)
entries.note: Bit-identical on the same build and platform. Native Linux and the web build agree on the shmup state hash.

entries.name: Replays (record, verify, seek)
entries.note: [REPLAYS.md](REPLAYS.md). Milestone 11.7a: actions have stable IDs (replay format 3; older files load by action name) and a backward seek in the editor resumes from a snapshot.

entries.name: Job system and SIMD kernels
entries.note: The same state hash for any thread count and with SIMD on or off.

entries.name: Particles (gameplay and visual modes)
entries.note: Gameplay mode is deterministic and collidable; see `cuervo/particles/README.md`.

entries.name: Collision (circles, capsules, spatial hash)
entries.note: AABB and OBB shapes are planned.

entries.name: Audio (miniaudio decoding, own mixer, buses, voice limiting)
entries.note: Per-bus effects and positional audio are planned.

entries.name: Node tree, scene files (versioned binary, text dump)
entries.note: [SCENES.md](SCENES.md).

entries.name: Node library (shapes, paths, sprites, text, camera, timer, area, emitter, audio player, lines, polygons)
entries.note: See [API.md](API.md).

entries.name: Transform hierarchy
entries.note: On by default; `[scene] transform_hierarchy = false` keeps world-space behavior.

entries.name: UI controls and widgets (containers, scroll, tabs, popups, `LineEdit`, ...)
entries.note: Keyboard, gamepad and pointer. No on-screen keyboard and no IME composition yet.

entries.name: Animation: `AnimationPlayer` (property, method and event tracks), `Tween`, `AnimationTree` state machine with cross-fades
entries.note: Time is in ticks and animations are saved in scene files; see [GUIDE.md](GUIDE.md) and [SCENES.md](SCENES.md). Replays include the values animation writes.

entries.name: Cutout, skeletal and morph animation, Bezier key handles, blend spaces, layered blending
entries.note: Not implemented. The track system is designed to carry cutout, skeletal and morph tracks (DESIGN.md 4.17).

entries.name: Tilemaps (`TileMapLayer`, autotiling, paint tool) and navigation (`NavigationRegion2D`, `NavigationAgent2D`)
entries.note: Milestone 9.5. Deterministic A* with strict tie-breaking; see [API.md](API.md).

entries.name: Physics (Box2D v3 scene-tree bodies)
entries.note: Milestone 9.6. Box2D v3 scene-tree bodies (StaticBody2D, CharacterBody2D, RigidBody2D, Area2D, CollisionShape2D), raycasts, joints; see [API.md](API.md).

entries.name: General ECS exposed to scripts
entries.note: Milestone 12.4 decides whether to expose it or drop it.

entries.name: Networking (lockstep, rollback), HTTP and WebSocket
entries.note: Milestone 11.1. Transport interface, seeded loopback, lockstep and rollback with snapshot-hash desync detection, a UDP transport, WebSocket (`ws://` and `wss://`) transports, a relay, the `Net` and `Http` APIs and end-to-end netplay. Games for up to four players run over UDP mesh or a relay. The web transport and the HTTP fetch path are checked in headless Chrome.

entries.name: Localization, save and settings API, accessibility features
entries.note: Milestones 11.3 and 11.4. `Locale` and `tr` for translation tables, plurals and number and date formatting, IME composition in `LineEdit`, typed save slots with versions and migrations, a `Settings` API and a Chrome-trace profiler. Web saves persist through IndexedDB. Accessibility features (12.3) are still to do.

sections.title: The Pluma language and its tools

entries.name: Bytecode VM, type checker, coroutines, signals, hot reload
entries.note: [LANGUAGE.md](LANGUAGE.md), [PLUMA_GUIDE.md](PLUMA_GUIDE.md).

entries.name: Collections, strings, `Result` and `?`, math, geometry, noise, seeded `Rng`
entries.note: The same results in the VM and in AOT.

entries.name: Memory model (refcounting, cycle collector, opt-in manual memory)
AOT-to-C compilation
entries.note: Host platform only: the export host must be the target (Linux or Windows). Needs a C compiler. On Windows the C compiler is LLVM clang with every toolchain (docs/WINDOWS.md). Not used for web exports (web games ship scripts as source); an AOT export for another platform is refused.

entries.name: Formatter, language server, VS Code extension
entries.note: `cuervo-tools fmt`, `cuervo-tools lsp`, [the extension](../tools/vscode-pluma/README.md). Host tools. On Windows the server puts stdio in binary mode so the `Content-Length` header is exact (`stdio_framing` test).

entries.name: Debugger (DAP) and profiler
entries.note: On the VM only; not available for AOT-native exports or the web. On Windows stdio is in binary mode so the `Content-Length` header is exact (`stdio_framing` test).

entries.name: Modules, `import` and packages
entries.note: Milestone 10.5b: `import`, `pub` across packages, `[dependencies]` with pinned versions (vendored or by path), packed into exports; see [PACKAGES.md](PACKAGES.md). `examples/garden` reaches its dev state hash from source and AOT packs on Linux, on Windows and in headless Chrome. Packages are shared through registries (10.5d).

entries.name: Unit tests (`@test`)
entries.note: Milestone 10.5b: `plm test` and `cuervo-tools test` run a game's or a package's `@test` functions, each in a fresh session; left out of builds. See [LANGUAGE.md](LANGUAGE.md) 9.27. Host tools.

entries.name: Plugin API, FFI, embedding
entries.note: Milestone 10.5c: native plugins over one C ABI (version 1) in C++, Rust and C# (.NET, desktop only), with nodes, natives and importers; C++ and Rust plugins link statically into AOT exports. `@extern` calls C functions ([LANGUAGE.md](LANGUAGE.md) 9.28); `pluma/embed/pluma_embed.h` hosts the VM from C. See [PLUGINS.md](PLUGINS.md). Not on the web yet.

entries.name: Editor (`cuervo-editor`, RmlUi)
entries.note: The default editor: scene tree, inspector, gizmos, fixed panel layout with named layouts, script editor with debugger, play-in-editor, replays, profiler. Desktop only; there is no web editor. Checked on Linux (Vulkan, GL). The Windows and macOS builds are not yet verified (CI results pending). See [editor/README.md](../editor/README.md).

entries.name: Dear ImGui editor (`cuervo-editor --imgui`, deprecated)
entries.note: Deprecated and planned for removal: the previous editor, kept behind `--imgui` and compiled out with `-DCUERVO_EDITOR_IMGUI=OFF`. Docking layouts and panels that move to their own OS windows exist only here. See [DESIGN.md 4.13](DESIGN.md).

entries.name: Export for Linux (source and AOT scripts, stripped players)
entries.note: Shared libraries (SDL3, and FreeType for full players) are not bundled. [EXPORT.md](EXPORT.md).

entries.name: Export for the web
entries.note: Needs an emsdk (6.0.12) and a host-tools build. Compatible tier only; a Full project is refused.

entries.name: Export for Windows (source and AOT scripts, stripped players)
entries.note: Ships the GUI-subsystem `cuervo-player.exe` of the build tree or a prebuilt package's export template. The shmup and the tutorial exported with source and AOT scripts reach their dev state hashes from another directory, with MSVC and MinGW-w64 players. Stripped players build on a Windows host (tictak's: -31 %, same hash). [EXPORT.md](EXPORT.md).

entries.name: Pack format (`game.pak`)
entries.note: Deterministic, integrity-checked, uncompressed (the web server compresses).

entries.name: Documentation site (`docs_site` target)
entries.note: Built from these Markdown files; every link is checked, and the support tables are checked against `docs/support.json`.

entries.name: Dev-only features (`--demo`, `--svg`, `--bench`)
entries.note: Not in stripped players.

entries.name: Package registry and `license report`
entries.note: Milestone 10.5d: `cuervo-tools plugin verify|publish|install|list` over a directory registry with SHA-256 checksums, SPDX license checks, engine and ABI version ranges and a conformance state hash for sim-safe plugins; `license report` and exports list the packages' licenses. See [PLUGINS.md](PLUGINS.md). HTTP registries are not built yet.

entries.name: Signed prebuilt editor and export templates
entries.note: Milestone 10.5a. The release workflow builds the editor, tools and players on a `v*` tag, with export templates in `templates/<platform>/`, a SHA-256 sum for every file (and a Sigstore attestation once the repository is public), and Authenticode signatures on the Windows executables when the repository has a signing certificate (docs/WINDOWS.md "Prebuilt binaries"). Released builds are attached to each `v*` tag of the public repository.

entries.name: Content tools (dialogue, timeline, particle and shader editors), AI tools
entries.note: Milestones 12.1 and 12.2.

compatible.summary: The portable tier and the default. A project that stays inside it runs unchanged on Vulkan, OpenGL 3.3, OpenGL ES 3.0 and WebGL2.
guarantees: Every Compatible RHI feature in the table below is available on every backend and platform that serves the tier.
The device is clamped to the limits above even when the hardware offers more, so a game tested on Vulkan cannot use what WebGL2 lacks.
The optional features (MSAA, frame capture) degrade instead of breaking a project when a device lacks them.
refuses: Custom shader constructs GLES 3.0 cannot express (storage buffers, image load/store, atomics, subgroups, bindless, 64-bit floats, ...): a tier check error.
Compute, geometry, tessellation, mesh and task shader stages: a tier check error.
Textures larger than the limit above (split them into an atlas): a tier check error.
Full-only RHI features: the gated device logs once and ignores the call.

full.summary: The desktop tier. Everything Compatible has, plus features only Vulkan provides. It is the migration target when a game outgrows WebGL2.
guarantees: Runs on the Vulkan backend on Linux and Windows only. Full has no fixed numeric minimums yet.
The Full RHI features in the table below are required: a Vulkan device missing one is refused.
refuses: The OpenGL backend: a Full project on GL, or on any device that cannot serve Full, is refused at startup with an error naming --backend vulkan.
The web: a Full project cannot be exported with --platform web (tier check and export both refuse it).
Exports for a platform this page does not list for the tier.
